items.title: claim-check --force-expire cross-agent overrides must run a structured abandoned-check (age + git activity + git stash signals) BEFORE accepting --really --reason, gating MEDIUM/LOW confidence on a two-part operator clearance (--operator-confirmed flag plus COA_OPERATOR=1 env)
acceptance: scripts/checks/claim-check.mjs exports checkClaimAbandoned({claim, gitCmd, stashCmd, now}) — pure function returning {abandoned, confidence, signals}. Three independent signals: age (alive if claim younger than MIN_FORCE_EXPIRE_AGE_MINUTES, abandoned otherwise), git activity (alive if gitCmd(['log','--author=<agent>','--since=<created>','--oneline']) returns commits, abandoned if stdout empty + status 0, unknown if status != 0 or cmd missing), git stash (alive if stashCmd(['list']) entry mentions claim.id or claim.agent, abandoned if entries exist but none match or list is empty, unknown if status != 0 or cmd missing). TTL-expired claims short-circuit to high-confidence abandoned.

Confidence aggregation rule — 'high' iff all three signals positively say abandoned and none say alive; 'low' if any signal positively says alive; 'medium' otherwise (some unknowns, no positive alive). 'high' is the only tier that lets cross-agent overrides flow through without operator clearance.
ABANDONED_CONFIDENCE constants ('high', 'medium', 'low') exported and Object.frozen so callers cannot mutate the tier vocabulary.

--force-expire CLI runs checkClaimAbandoned only on the cross-agent classification path (decision.classification === 'cross-agent'). Same-agent and young-claim-override classifications skip the new check — the agent acting on its own claim already knows its state, so TPL-221's Layer A/C semantics are preserved unchanged.

--operator-confirmed flag is a NEW CLI argument. Must be paired with COA_OPERATOR=1 in the calling shell environment. Flag without env is rejected with an explicit "agents cannot fake this" message. Env without flag is rejected because the operator must explicitly opt in for each invocation.

LOW or MEDIUM confidence + no operator clearance → hard reject with exit 1, structured rejection message naming the confidence tier and listing the signals the script saw, and a 'force-expire-rejected' audit event with rejectionReason = 'abandoned-check-low' or 'abandoned-check-medium'. Claim status stays 'active'. Pre-fix, --really --reason on a 2-min-old claim succeeded (Field-finding-012 incident); post-fix the same call is rejected.

HIGH confidence cross-agent override succeeds with just --really --reason (preserves the canonical TPL-221 "old claim, no signs of life" path) and the audit event embeds the abandonedCheck signals so an operator can later reconstruct the decision facts.

buildAuditEvent gains optional abandonedCheck + operatorConfirmed parameters. When present they materialize as a nested abandonedCheck:{abandoned, confidence, signals, operatorConfirmed} object on the audit event. When absent the event shape stays exactly TPL-221 (back-compat for same-agent events). Signals array is cloned to defend against caller mutation.

Cross-agent rejections by the abandoned-check write a 'force-expire-rejected' audit event with the rejectionReason, abandonedCheck, and operatorConfirmed fields. This is a NEW event type — TPL-221 wrote no audit on rejection.

tests/unit/claim-check.test.mjs adds a checkClaimAbandoned describe block (12 tests covering TTL fast path, all-abandoned → high, alive-signal → low, recent-commits → low, stash-id-match → low, stash-agent-match → low, all-unknown → medium, gitCmd-throws-stays-unknown, null-claim → low + descriptive signal, frozen constants) plus 4 new buildAuditEvent tests covering abandonedCheck embedding, omission for back-compat, operatorConfirmed=true, and signals-array cloning. items.title: claim-check --auto-complete --staged must reject when HEAD has not moved (J3), must require --agent and gate cross-agent completion behind --really + --reason (J3.5), and must exclude auto-extended ceremony targets from the must-be-in-proof-set check (J3.6)
acceptance: scripts/checks/claim-check.mjs --auto-complete --staged refuses with exit 1 when no caller agent can be resolved (no --agent, no $COA_AGENT, no auto-detect from active claim covering the staged set). The refusal is the J3.5 Layer A defense and is exactly the sibling of TPL-221's --force-expire Layer A.

Same-agent-only by default — when --agent=<X> is provided, only claims with claim.agent === X are considered for completion. Foreign claims that happen to have their targets covered by the proof set are silently skipped and audit-logged with rejectionReason "agent-mismatch", so the J3.5 incident (B's commit falsely completing A's claim) is now both prevented and observable.

Cross-agent escape — passing --really --reason="<text>" expands the candidate set to include foreign claims; --really without --reason is a hard rejection (rejectionReason "cross-agent-no-reason"). Successful cross-agent completions write audit events with crossAgent=true and the supplied reason.

HEAD verification (J3) — auto-complete refuses to flip a claim's status to "completed" without one of three trust signals: (1) --commit-hash=<H> exists in git log AND its commit covers the claim's user (non-extended) targets; (2) --from-pre-commit-hook flag (privileged short-circuit used by .githooks/pre-commit's post-success block); (3) HEAD's most recent commit covers the claim's user targets. If none holds, exit 1 with a clear message naming each escape hatch.

J3.6 — claim targets carrying `extended: true` (added by TPL-222's tryExtendClaim during coa-merge ceremony) are *aspirational* coverage. findCompletableClaims excludes them from the "all targets must be in proof set" subset check, and verifyClaimWorkCommitted excludes them from the "commit must include all targets" check. A claim with only extended targets is NOT completable (no user-acquired anchor).
tryExtendClaim now stamps every newly-added target with extended: true so coa-merge ceremony auto-extension is distinguishable from user-acquired targets at completion time.

Pre-commit-hook agent fallback — when --from-pre-commit-hook is supplied without --agent, claim-check resolves the caller agent in this order: (1) $COA_AGENT env var; (2) the most recent active claim whose targets intersect the staged set; (3) refuse. The fallback path lets the bash hook stay simple while still attaching an agent identity.

--commit-hash=<H> changes the candidate-source set: the post-commit operator flow has an empty staging set, so claim-check uses the commit's diff-tree as the candidate source instead. --staged remains the source when --from-pre-commit-hook or no commit-hash is supplied.

verifyClaimWorkCommitted({ claim, gitCmd, commitHash, fromPreCommitHook }) and verifyAgentAuthorization({ claim, callerAgent, hasReally, reason }) are exported as pure helpers; the CLI handler is a thin shell over them. gitCmd is injectable for unit tests.

Every accept/skip/reject appends a structured event to .claims/audit.log. Schema for auto-complete: { ts, event, claimId, claimAgent, claimSlice, callerAgent, agentSource, verifiedBy, commitHash, agentMatch, crossAgent, reason }. Schema for auto-complete-rejected adds rejectionReason ∈ { "agent-mismatch", "cross-agent-no-reason", "head-did-not-move", "target-mismatch" }.

tests/unit/claim-check.test.mjs adds three describe blocks (verifyAgentAuthorization, verifyClaimWorkCommitted, findCompletableClaims J3.6) covering the eight-plus authorization paths, the six J3 verification paths, and three J3.6 extended-target paths (23 new tests; 205 total).

tests/integration/claim-check-collision-rehearsal.test.mjs adds twelve scenarios reproducing J3 (uncommitted auto-complete rejected; commit-hash success), J3.5 (no --agent rejected; same-agent success; foreign-agent skip with audit; cross-agent --really --reason success; --really without --reason rejected; B-commits-A-mid-work composite), J3.6 (extended-target ceremony completes; user-target absent rejects), pre-commit-hook short-circuit, COA_AGENT env-driven derivation, and active-claim auto-detect.

items.title: coa-merge must be atomic across the version-bump + commit window so a mid-pipeline failure cannot leave VERSION/CHANGELOG/package.json mutated without an accompanying commit, must detect that residue on next start, must auto-extend the caller's claim with ceremony+regen paths so Phase-3 enforcement passes, and must emit a half-baked-state marker on commit failure
acceptance: J2 pre-flight detect-and-resume — when working tree VERSION is exactly +1 from HEAD AND CHANGELOG already has the [wtVersion] section AND [Unreleased] is empty, coa-merge refuses to start at step 0 with copy-pasteable recovery instructions (resume = re-stage + git commit; abort = git restore VERSION CHANGELOG.md package.json).

J5 auto-extend before enforce — coa-merge step 2.5 finds the caller's most-recently-created active claim that intersects user-staged files, and extends it with VERSION + package.json + CHANGELOG.md + Phase-5 regen paths (AGENTS.md, .cursorrules, LOCAL.md, MICRO.md, docs/_generated/dependency-graph.json, docs/_generated/spec-index.json, docs/backlog/_generated/index.md, docs/backlog/_generated/backlog.json) before pre-commit Phase 3 runs. Missing claim fails step 2.5 with a clear "your slice needs --acquire first" message.

claim-check --extend CLI — same-agent only (no cross-agent escape; cross-agent rejected outright), validates target paths, caps at MAX_TARGETS, idempotent on already-covered paths, appends audit-log event with addedTargets[] and crossAgent:false.

J1 deferred mutation + rollback — VERSION, package.json, and CHANGELOG.md are computed in memory at steps 4-6 and only written immediately before staging at step 7. If pre-commit at step 8 fails, rollbackCeremonyFiles() restores all three from `git show HEAD:<path>` and unstages them; the operator's user-file staging is preserved.

J4 half-baked-state marker — failures at step ≥4 (mutation territory) emit `.cockpit/markers/half-baked-<timestamp>.json` with `type: "half-baked-commit"`, `stepFailed`, `headVersion`, `workingTreeVersion`, `changelogReleased`, `claimId`, `agent`, and a `recoveryHint`. Pure helpers exported for unit testing — detectPartialState({headVersion, wtVersion, changelogText}) returning {partial, kind, headVersion, wtVersion}; resolveAutoExtendPaths({filesUserStaged, ceremonyFiles, regenPaths}) returning the path list; hasVersionedSection(text, version); tryExtendClaim({claim, callerAgent, addTargets, action}); DEFAULT_CEREMONY_FILES; DEFAULT_REGEN_PATHS.

tests/unit/coa-merge.test.mjs adds 18 tests across hasVersionedSection / detectPartialState / resolveAutoExtendPaths covering normal, half-baked, partial, defensive, dedup, normalization, and Phase-5 regen membership.

tests/unit/claim-check.test.mjs adds 15 tests for tryExtendClaim covering same-agent, cross-agent rejection, missing/whitespace --agent, traversal/absolute path, inactive-claim status check, null claim, invalid action, idempotency, dedup, no-op, MAX_TARGETS overflow, and Windows path normalization.

tests/integration/parallel-sessions.test.mjs adds 5 scenarios — half-baked pre-flight refusal with helpful message, normal state pre-flight passes, --extend same-agent end-to-end with claim file rewrite, --extend cross-agent rejected and claim file untouched, --extend audit-log event written, coa-merge auto-extends the caller's claim before Phase 3 with VERSION/CHANGELOG/package.json/AGENTS.md, no-claim case fails step 2.5 with --acquire usage hint.

items.title: claim-check --force-expire must enforce a multi-layer authorization model so a sibling session cannot unilaterally wipe a live claim without identifying itself, justifying the override, or leaving an audit trail
acceptance: scripts/checks/claim-check.mjs --force-expire requires --agent=<X> from every caller; missing --agent is rejected with exit 1 and a usage message that documents the required flags. Pre-fix the request was accepted silently from any caller — that silence was the security defect.

claimAgeSeconds(claim, now), validateForceExpireRequest({claim, callerAgent, hasReally, reason, now}), buildAuditEvent(...), and MIN_FORCE_EXPIRE_AGE_MINUTES are exported as pure helpers; the CLI handler is a thin shell over them.

items.title: Move dependency-graph regeneration into pre-commit Phase 5 and auto-stage regenerated _generated artefacts so sibling worktrees stop failing on stale dep-graph

items.title: Measure each module's work-surface tokens and gate against the local-LLM 16K context floor with a data-driven warn threshold
acceptance: scripts/checks/module-fit-check.mjs measures each modules/<name>/'s work surface (manifest + public-api + sidecars + one representative impl + one representative test) using Math.ceil(bytes/4) as the token approximation and exports pure helpers (approximateTokenCount, pickRepresentativeImpl, pickRepresentativeTest, measureWorkSurface, computeDistribution, discoverModuleNames) for direct unit testing.
